messages.author: 294ba97ff99e9970
messages.subject: MVPA threshold for adults
parts:
Hi GGIR users, 

I used the MVPA threshold of 100.6 defined by Hildebrand et al. (2014) for my rural adults. However, this threshold seemed too low as many of my participants generated more than 200 mins MVPA/day, but they did not think they were so active. Does anyone have any suggestions for other MVPA thresholds? 

Thanks in advance, 
Mothu

messages.author: 5636dac60e2efbc1
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] MVPA threshold for adults
parts:
Hello,

I find it surprising that you had participants who thought they were not very active, but had over 200 minutes of MVPA per day. From my experience, it is quite common to get 0 minutes MVPA per day (at Hildebrand threshold) with participants who are not active.  Are you sure that your raw acceleration data is being saved in g-units? This large amount of MVPA might be happening if your raw data is  in m/s/s, so would probably be worth investigating that as a first step.

Matt

messages.author: 294ba97ff99e9970
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] MVPA threshold for adults
parts:
Hi Matt, 

I did use raw data to process. For my MVPA, I defined it as AD_MVPA_E5S_T100.6_ENMO. Not sure how did you define your MVPA, but if you defined it the same as me, I do not think 0 mins of MVPA is possible as 100.6 threshold is quite low. Instead, if you used AD_MVPA_E5S_B10M80%_T100.6_ENMO_0-24hr, it is highly possible to get 0 mins of MVPA.

messages.author: c98af2c83883e808
messages.subject: Re: MVPA threshold for adults
parts:
Hi,

Using the total does tend to return quite high values for MVPA. For this reason some groups use 1 min bouts of MVPA. For example, Menai et al used 1 min bouts with the Whitehall data and state:'To remove signals related to random wrist movement, we only retained activities
lasting at least 1 minute for which 80% of the activity satisfied the 100 mg threshold criteria.' (https://www.nature.com/articles/srep45772). 

Alex
